messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Threat
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Threat → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Threat → Negative Appraisals
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Negative Appraisals
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Triggers
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Threat

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

The night everything fractured began during a routine server migration at Tariq Al-Mansour’s downtown engineering firm. He had stayed late to troubleshoot a database collapse, only to be cornered in the loading bay by a visiting IT auditor who pinned him to the damp pavement. The assault was over quickly, but the sensory imprints never faded; the muffled wail of a police siren and the flashing lights of an approaching ambulance that night became permanently fused with the terror of being trapped alone with a man in a position of power. As those auditory alarms and the sight of passing ambulances continued to sound in his peripheral world, Tariq found himself systematically retreating from the environments that once defined his career. He stopped attending evening stakeholder meetings to evade authority figures in tailored suits, bypassed the east wing of his office to avoid the location where the attack occurred, and turned down consulting gigs that required working alone in conference rooms with male clients. The constant pull of those external cues dictated his withdrawal. His nervous system rarely granted him reprieve, firing false alarms during routine fire drills and mistaking delivery trucks for pursuing engines. Because his body continued to react as if he were being hunted, the avoidance became a rigid survival architecture, manifesting in his refusal to walk past the city hospital and his insistence on checking twice for uniforms before leaving his apartment. This internal danger signal corroded his sense of self, leading him to interpret his physiological panic as confirmation that he had invited the violation. The injustice of the assault and the absence of consequences for his attacker settled into a heavy narrative that framed the world as fundamentally hostile. Those corrosive beliefs soon dictated his daily habits. Believing the event was entirely his fault and that he would never recover his emotional capacity, Tariq doubled down on his isolation. He declined remote collaboration invites to avoid digital contact with male colleagues and requested desk changes away from the open-plan tech floor to sidestep encounters with anyone in uniform. The more he fortified his routines, the more the convictions hardened. By removing himself from situations where resolution could emerge, he guaranteed that his culpability narrative and emotional numbness would remain unchallenged. Every closed door simply fed back into his certainty that he was fundamentally broken. This quarantine inadvertently magnified his original sensitivities. Because he never allowed his nervous system to habituate, the avoidance patterns kept his threat detectors perpetually primed. He flinched at every distant siren and the sight of a delivery van, his panic escalating precisely because he had never tested his safety against these stimuli. The very strategies meant to protect him now guaranteed that every cue would trigger fresh physiological alarms. At thirty-four weeks of relentless hyperarousal, this pattern closed in on his professional life. His constant scanning for danger and rigid safe-zone dependency caused him to misread routine code reviews as hostile interrogations. A final warning email regarding his unexplained absences from sprint planning forced him into a therapist’s office. Now, sitting across from the clinician, Tariq admits that while the external world remains crowded with potential violators, the internal landscape is far more treacherous. He is terrified that seeking help will only expose his lingering fragility, yet he is equally exhausted by the emotional numbness that has calcified around his chest. He hopes, with a quiet and weary certainty, that someone can help him untangle false alarms from the truth of what actually happened, and that he might eventually learn to inhabit his own body without bracing for the next assault.
